hard_constraints.rationale: ASSUMPTION: footprints with median elevation above +2 km leave too little atmosphere for current EDL architectures. Historical mission limits were lower; this is a permissive screening bound.

ASSUMPTION: the 2015 NASA First Landing Site / Exploration Zone Workshop for human missions screened candidate zones to within 50 degrees of the equator for solar power and thermal reasons. Applied here as a documented default, not as a rule for robotic landers.

criteria.label: Terrain safety (regional slope)
criteria.rationale: Lower regional slopes reduce the chance that a landing ellipse spans tilted terrain such as crater walls or rises. The 2 deg 'fully suitable' knee and the 10 deg cut-off are screening assumptions at the ~3.7 km baseline. Recent landing-site selections set slope limits at much shorter baselines: slopes <15 deg at 84 m and 2 m length scales for InSight (Golombek et al., 2017) and <30 deg at 2-5 m baselines for MSL (Golombek et al., 2012), which MEGDR 16 ppd slopes (~3.7 km baseline) cannot resolve.

criteria.label: Elevation suitability (EDL atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Lower elevation means a thicker atmospheric column for entry, descent and landing deceleration. Recent engineering limits: elevation <-1 km for MSL (Golombek et al., 2012) and <=-2.5 km for InSight (Golombek et al., 2017); for Perseverance, with new EDL capabilities, elevation and latitude limits no longer decided site viability (Grant et al., 2018). The -3000 m / +2000 m knees are a screening assumption spanning that range; +2 km is also the preliminary elevation limit for human Exploration Zones (Bussey & Hoffman, 2016). A real mission's limit depends on its EDL system.

criteria.label: Surface roughness (detrended relief)
criteria.rationale: Standard deviation of MOLA elevation within the footprint after removing a best-fit plane. Low values indicate smooth plains at the km scale; high values indicate crater rims, scarps or hummocky terrain. Knees are assumptions tuned so smooth plains score near 1 and crater-wall-dominated footprints score near 0. Not a proxy for rock abundance or decimetre-scale roughness.

criteria.label: Thermal conditions
criteria.rationale: Warmer mean surface temperatures ease thermal management for landed hardware. PLACEHOLDER: no Mars site carries this feature in profile v1 (THEMIS/TES integration is an open Engineer-2 task), so under the common_feature_set policy this criterion is excluded and reported in completeness rather than scored.

criteria.label: Solar illumination (annual mean, top of atmosphere)
criteria.rationale: Annual-mean top-of-atmosphere insolation computed from latitude and Mars orbital elements (see SCIENTIFIC_METHOD.md). The knees are the physical range of the feature under the pipeline's own model (scripts/geo.py): the equatorial annual mean is 178.6 W/m2 and the polar annual mean 79.8 W/m2, so `full` = 178 makes an equatorial site fully suitable and `zero` = 80 makes a polar site unsuitable. (An earlier 185 W/m2 knee was S_Mars/pi = 186.6 W/m2 without obliquity, a value no latitude attains, so q = 1 was unreachable - corrected 2026-11-14.) Ignores atmospheric dust opacity and local horizon, so it is a latitude-driven proxy for solar power availability, not a surface measurement.

research_studies.title: Does the regional terrain statistic predict landing-scale hazards at Jezero Crater?
research_studies.research_question: Do the ~3.7 km MOLA slope and relief values that rank Jezero Crater here (median slope 1.077 deg, detrended relief 194.4 m) correspond to metre-scale slopes and rock hazards inside a realistic landing ellipse?
research_studies.method: Sample HiRISE/CTX-derived digital terrain models at 1-5 m baselines over the footprint, count rocks from HiRISE images, and compare the distributions with the regional MOLA statistics used by this tool.
research_studies.why_here: Jezero Crater has a complete regional terrain profile and retrieved documentation of the topographic data and its sampling caveats, so the comparison can be made without new orbital data.
research_studies.cannot_infer: Regional statistics cannot resolve lander-scale hazards, and the suitability score is a screening index; neither establishes that a landing would be safe.

research_studies.title: Record of past water at Jezero Crater: carbonates, delta, paleolake basin
research_studies.research_question: What depositional or alteration history produced the carbonates, delta, paleolake basin reported for Jezero Crater, and how well are those materials preserved for in-situ or returned-sample analysis?
research_studies.method: Targeted orbital spectroscopy (CRISM) over the footprint to map the cited units, then in-situ or returned-sample mineralogy and organic chemistry on the mapped outcrops.
research_studies.why_here: The cited literature for Jezero Crater documents these materials, and the retrieved passages describe their setting, so the hypotheses are specific rather than generic.
research_studies.cannot_infer: Composition tags are literature-derived labels, not spectral measurements made by this tool, and they have no bearing on the landing suitability score.

research_studies.title: Field rehearsal at Jaroso Ravine on terrain it shares with Jezero Crater
research_studies.research_question: Do traverse-planning and terrain-mapping methods exercised at Jaroso Ravine transfer to the Jezero Crater landforms they share?
research_studies.method: Run instrumented traverses and terrain mapping on the matched landforms at the Earth site, measure where predicted and observed trafficability diverge, then test the method on orbital data for the Mars footprint.
research_studies.why_here: Shared at the harmonised ~3.7 km baseline: Regional slope: Mars 1.08 deg vs Earth 1.06 deg (difference 0.02 deg, within half the 1.50 deg comparison scale).
research_studies.cannot_infer: The similarity index (68.54) is a heuristic; Earth gravity, atmosphere and radiation differ, and no transfer has been demonstrated.
